sections.label: Loss Carry-Back Relief extension
sections.summary: The enhanced Loss Carry-Back Relief scheme is extended one year, allowing qualifying deductions for YA 2021 to be carried back up to three preceding YAs, capped at $100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, to help businesses with cash flow, the enhancement to the Loss Carry-Back Relief scheme has been extended for another year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Qualifying deductions for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2021 may be carried back up to three preceding YAs, instead of one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amount of qualifying deductions that may be carried back is capped at $100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This allows businesses to get a refund of up to $17,000 of income tax paid for YA 2018 to YA 2020.

sections.label: IRAS access to income tax data
sections.summary: The amendment lets persons authorised by the CEO of IRAS access selected income tax data and documents, safeguarded, solely to audit the administration of public schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As the Income Tax Act restricts the disclosure of protected income tax data to non-public servants including external auditors, this amendment will allow persons authorised by the CEO of IRAS access to selected income tax data and documents, appropriately safeguarded, for the sole purpose of auditing the administration of public schemes.

sections.label: GST access and informer protection
sections.summary: The Goods and Services Tax Act is amended to allow authorised persons access to GST information, and a protection of informers provision is included.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a related amendment, we will also amend the Goods and Services Tax Act to allow access to Goods and Services Tax information to persons authorised by the CEO of IRAS to audit the administration of public schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, a protection of informers provision will be included, similar to the provision in legislation like the Customs Act and the Cybersecurity Act 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This amendment protects informers by prohibiting witnesses in Court, who might be the informers themselves, from disclosing information that may lead to the discovery of an informer’s identity and thus encourages informers to step forward with information that will enable more effective tax enforcement.

sections.label: Donation tax deduction scheme extension
sections.summary: The Bill extends by two years the end date of the scheme providing tax deductions for qualifying donations up until the end of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To encourage this, the Government is providing tax deductions for qualifying donations up until the end of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill extends the end date of that scheme by two years.

sections.label: Donations to DAFs growth
sections.summary: From 2015 to 2019, donations to DAFs rose by 110% in the UK and 80% in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 2015 to 2019, donations to DAFs have risen by 110% in the UK and 80% in the US.

sections.label: Income tax deductions for DAF donations
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for the yearly dollar amount of income tax deductions linked with donations to DAFs for each of the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister share what is the yearly dollar amount of income tax deductions linked with donations to DAFs for each of the past five years?

sections.label: Purpose of new section 14ZH
sections.summary: The passage states that the purpose of the new section 14ZH is unclear in this context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this context, the purpose of the new section 14ZH is unclear.

sections.label: Projected revenue loss from provisions
sections.summary: The passage asks what the projected loss in revenue from the proposed provisions and tax exemptions is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the projected loss in revenue from the proposed provisions and tax exemptions?

sections.label: Packaging framework roadblocks and targeted tax rebates
sections.summary: The passage notes the Mandatory Packaging Reporting Framework hit COVID-19 roadblocks and proposes a more targeted approach for specific tax rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us not forget that the recently introduced Mandatory Packaging Reporting Framework under the Resource Sustainability Act, which was intended to help companies reduce packaging use, had also hit roadblocks due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would propose a more targeted approach to identify relevant sectors and businesses for specific tax rebates.

sections.label: IRAS verifying declared expenses validity
sections.summary: The passage asks how IRAS would determine the validity of declared expenses to ensure they are not frivolous or fictitious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moreover, how would IRAS determine the validity of declared expenses to ensure that they are not frivolous, or worse, fictitious?

sections.label: Similar provisions and whistle-blower protection
sections.summary: The passage asks whether similar provisions will be introduced to other corporate crime statutes and whether whistle-blower protection clauses will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government introduce similar provisions to other statutes concerned with corporate crime?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government also consider enhancing the current whistle-blower protection clauses to prohibit corporations from retaliating against whistle-blowers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The current provision only protects informers from being identified in proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, it does not stop a company who is aware of a whistle-blower complaint, from initiating a witch-hunt to flush out the whistle-blower.

sections.label: Poorly timed GST hike effects
sections.summary: The passage states that a poorly timed GST hike would reduce consumer activity and hurt businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A poorly timed GST hike would lead to reduced consumer activity, which in turn hurts businesses.

sections.label: 250% tax deduction extension
sections.summary: Clause 29 amends section 37 to extend the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations to IPCs and other recipients for donations from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, in relation to the proposed amendments included in the Bill, clause 29 amends section 37, where the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations made to IPCs and other qualifying recipients will be extended for another two years, that is, for donations made during the period 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2023.

sections.label: Permanent 250% donation deduction
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations to IPCs should be made permanent to encourage sustainable giving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To better encourage sustainable giving by Singaporeans and companies here, where the habit of giving is integrated into our lives, should we not make permanent the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations made to IPCs?

sections.label: IRAS records access for audits
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends section 6 to let a person authorised by the Comptroller of Income Tax access IRAS records and taxpayer income documents to audit public schemes in the Ninth Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, clause 2 amends section 6 to allow any person authorised by the Comptroller of Income Tax access to any IRAS records and all documents containing taxpayer income information protected under section 6 that are necessary for the person to audit IRAS administration of any public scheme specified in the Ninth Schedule.

sections.label: New section 10P tax treatment
sections.summary: A new section 10P provides tax treatment when trading stock is appropriated for non-trade or capital purposes and when non-trade or capital assets become trading stock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I note the creation of a new section 10P which provides the tax treatment for cases where trading stock is appropriated for non-trade or capital purposes, and where non-trade or capital asset becomes trading stock.

sections.label: Private versus HDB price gap
sections.summary: The passage states private home prices rose more than HDB resale prices over recent periods and that the share of resident households in public housing fell to 78.7% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, private home prices rose 10.9% between end-2020 and end-2015, while HDB resale prices only rose by 2.4% over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if we take into account the sharp spike in HDB resale prices year-to-date, HDB resale prices rose by 11.7% in the past five years compared to 19.7% for private home prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This wealth gap has been exacerbated by the falling percentage of resident households who live in public housing, which has declined to 78.7% in 2020, from 80% in 2015 and 82% in 2010.

sections.label: Taxing high-value properties
sections.summary: The passage suggests raising property-related taxes on homes valued above $5 million or on owners of multiple properties cumulatively worth $5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One possible solution is to raise property-related taxes on the homes valued above a high threshold, say, $5 million, or for owners of multiple properties cumulatively worth $5 million.

sections.label: SME corporate income tax rates
sections.summary: An SME with $300,000 chargeable income pays about $34,000 tax, an effective rate of about 11%, versus about $25,000 under prior rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For an SME making $300,000 in chargeable income, for example, total corporate income tax paid before any rebates will be close to $34,000 or an effective rate of about 11%, compared to around $25,000 or an effective rate of about 8% based on prior rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I recognise that Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong has said that effective tax rates for SMEs are much lower than the effective tax rates for non-SMEs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But what is also true is that SMEs paid $4.8 billion in corporate income tax out of profit before tax of $44 billion for YA2019 versus non-SMEs, which paid $11.5 billion in corporate tax out of profit before tax of $459 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Now, I do appreciate that MOF has its way of calculating effective tax rates, which the Finance Minister has clarified is based on a definition of chargeable income that is a bit different from that per section 38 of the Income Tax Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, using the data provided to my Parliamentary Question yesterday, for example, based on the subset of profit-making firms in YA2019, SMEs accounted for 20% of accounting profit before tax, 22% of chargeable income but 30% of corporate income tax paid.

sections.label: BEPS global minimum tax rate
sections.summary: With the current average effective corporate tax rate near 3%, a small shift toward the proposed 15% global minimum rate could raise corporate tax receipts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I recognise that a lot of details on BEPS implementation are still being ironed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But given the current average effective corporate tax rate is close to 3% as shared by the Minister, technically it would seem that even a small shift towards the proposed global minimum rate of 15% could result in much higher corporate tax receipts for the Government.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme and DTDi amendments
sections.summary: The amendments exempt Jobs Support Scheme payouts from income tax and enhance the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme with additional qualifying expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Amendment of section 13ZA: I thank the Government for its compassion towards the companies by exempting the Jobs Support Scheme payouts from income tax during this challenging time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Amendment of sections 14B and 14K: the Ministry proposes to enhance the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDi) scheme to include additional qualifying expenses in support of efforts made by our enterprises to go international.

sections.label: Accelerated plant and machinery write-off
sections.summary: The amendment extends the option to accelerate the write-off of plant and machinery acquisition costs to capital expenditure incurred in FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Amendment of section 19A: the Ministry seeks to extend the option to accelerate the write-off of the cost of acquiring plant and machinery to capital expenditure incurred in Financial Year (FY) 2021.

sections.label: Extension of donations tax deduction
sections.summary: The 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations is extended for another two years to 31 December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Amendment of section 37: to continue to encourage donations, the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations will be extended for another two years to 31 December 2023.

sections.label: Renovation and Refurbishment deduction option
sections.summary: The R&R measure lets taxpayers claim deductions on qualifying expenditure over one year instead of three, with the $300,000 cap unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, the Renovation and Refurbishment (R&R) measure mentioned by Mr Yip, allows taxpayers the option to claim tax deductions on qualifying expenditure over one year, instead of the three years which is already allowed under the Income Tax Act today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we are just allowing now one year instead of three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is also no change to the overall cap of $300,000, which applies for every relevant period of three consecutive Years of Assessment.

sections.label: DTDi scheme expense cap
sections.summary: The overall cap stays at $150,000 per year for qualifying expenses claimable without Enterprise Singapore's prior approval under the DTDi scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Again, the overall cap remains unchanged at $150,000 per year for the list of qualifying expenses which taxpayers can claim in their tax return without the prior approval of Enterprise Singapore under the DTDi scheme.

sections.label: Enhanced support for enterprise schemes
sections.summary: Budget this year extended enhanced support levels of up to 80% for existing enterprise schemes like the Productivity Solutions Grant and Enterprise Development Grant to end of March 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, in Budget this year, we had extended the enhanced support levels of up to 80% for existing enterprise schemes like the Productivity Solutions Grant and the Enterprise Development Grant, to end of March 2022.

sections.label: DAF disbursement and reporting rules
sections.summary: DAFs must disburse tax-deductible donations to IPCs within five years, except endowment funds, and all grant-makers submit annual reports to IRAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For such DAFs, they are required to disburse the tax-deductible donations to IPCs within five years from receiving the donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The only exception is when an endowment fund is being set up by the approved grant-maker, in which case the approved grant-maker can disburse the tax-deductible donations to IPCs over a longer period, obviously because they are setting up an endowment fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To ensure accountability, all grant-makers are required to submit annual reports to IRAS on the tax-deductible donations received and disbursed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Thus far, all grant-makers have disbursed the donations received to IPCs according to the disbursement requirements within the specified number of years.

sections.label: Tiered donation tax deduction proposal
sections.summary: Mr Wee proposed tiering tax deduction rates by donation quantum, but such a system would primarily benefit higher-income donors and larger IPCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the issue of tax deductions for donations, Mr Wee had proposed for the Government to tier the tax deduction rates based on the donation quantum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I understand the intent of such a suggestion but such a tiered system would then primarily benefit the higher-income as well as larger IPCs who have the resources to engage higher-income donors.

sections.label: Audits of IRAS payouts
sections.summary: Audits independently check that IRAS disburses payouts correctly to intended beneficiaries, with data limited to what is necessary for quality assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The audits provide independent checks to ensure IRAS disburses payouts correctly to their intended beneficiaries and the data provided to auditors will be limited to what is necessary for quality assurance of that specific scheme.

sections.label: Data not identifiable
sections.summary: The data made available will not be identifiable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More importantly, as I mentioned earlier in my speech, the data made available will not be identifiable.

sections.label: Secrecy declaration for authorised persons
sections.summary: Authorised persons accessing protected data must make a declaration of secrecy, and disclosing protected information is an offence under the ITA and Official Secrets Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Authorised persons who are granted access to protected data would be required to make and subscribe to a declaration of secrecy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It would be an offence under the ITA and the Official Secrets Act for authorised persons to disclose any protected information to other parties.

sections.label: Court disclosure of informer identity
sections.summary: The Court may require the original complaint and disclosure of the informer's identity only if satisfied of a wilfully false material statement or that justice cannot be done without it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In particular, the safeguard provides that the Court may require the production of the original complaint and full disclosure of the informer's identity only if the Court is satisfied that the informer wilfully made in his complaint a material statement which he knew or believed to be false or did not believe to be true; or justice cannot be fully done between the parties without the disclosure of the informer's identity.

sections.label: SMEs pay little tax
sections.summary: The vast majority of SMEs pay very little tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because, in fact, the vast majority of SMEs, vast majority of them, pay very little tax.

sections.label: GST rate increase timing
sections.summary: Rising recurrent expenditures require higher recurrent revenues, and the announced GST rate increase during 2022 to 2025 remains unchanged, with timing decided by fiscal needs and economic conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As our recurrent expenditures continue to go up for a whole range of reasons, including rapidly ageing population, the need for more healthcare, to make growing demands for social spending, then we have to ensure that we look at raising our recurrent revenues to meet these recurrent expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government has announced that the GST rate increase will take place sometime during 2022 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This remains unchanged and we will continue to consider all factors, including our fiscal needs as well as the prevailing economic conditions in deciding on the timing of the GST rate increase.
